newsitem.title: USA: U.S. expects Arafat to attend meeting.
newsitem.headline: U.S. expects Arafat to attend meeting.

text.p: The U.S. coordinator for Middle East peace talks on Monday said the United States still expects Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to come to Washington for a summit this week.

"We expect him to be here," said State Department official Dennis Ross when asked on NBC television's "Today" show if the United States would agree to delay the talks because of Arafat's apparent reluctance to come.
"The president issued an invitation to Chairman Arafat. Chairman Arafat agreed to come. We expect him to be here," Ross said.
"The next step is obviously to continue to talk with him but to have him come here. The fact is that we have seen hesitation before when we had big meetings," Ross said.
Arafat has asked Clinton to delay the proposed summit in Washington with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu until differences over the agenda were settled, PLO officials said.
